primarySection.hubTitle: StataNow 19.5 SE Consensus Synthesis & Forest Plots Hub
primarySection.hubText: Locked Protocol Synthesis Standard: In accordance with our PROSPERO protocol, TEAS and electroacupuncture (EA) are evaluated both in prespecified modality strata and in an overall consensus synthesis. Primary comparisons evaluate active stimulation versus credible sham/control. Between-study variance is estimated using restricted maximum likelihood (REML) with Knapp–Hartung confidence intervals and 95% prediction intervals.
primarySection.section2ATitle: Co-Primary Acute Window — Cumulative 0–24h Opioid Sparing (k = 11 RCTs, N = 945)
primarySection.section2ASub: Executed in StataNow 19.5 SE via meta summarize, random(reml) se(kh) predinterval.
primarySection.eaStratum: Primary Stratum 2: EA vs Control / Sham
primarySection.threshold10mgNotice: Primary prespecified clinical-importance threshold: 10 mg IV MME. The pooled average (−5.04 mg) does not reach the 10 mg threshold, though high-demand surgical cohorts achieve substantial sparing (12–22 mg).

metaregStudio.title: StataNow 19.5 SE Meta-Regression & Moderator Studio
metaregStudio.subtitle: Knapp–Hartung Random-Effects Meta-Regression exploring sources of clinical and methodological heterogeneity across the 11 primary trials.
metaregStudio.ruleOf10Text: The analysis meets a commonly used minimum study-count rule of thumb for exploratory univariable meta-regression (k = 11, 1 predictor), but statistical power may remain limited and results should be considered exploratory or hypothesis-generating.
metaregStudio.tableTitle: Comprehensive Moderator & Clinical Parameter Matrix (k = 11 Primary RCTs)
metaregStudio.cardEcologicalText: Meta-regression uses study-level averages or proportions. A relationship observed between studies does not necessarily represent the relationship between individual patients within those studies (Simpson's paradox). Evaluating individual patient age, BMI, or sex effects requires Individual Participant Data (IPD) meta-analysis.
metaregStudio.cardStrictaText: In accordance with STRICTA guidelines, acupoints in perioperative anesthesia trials are delivered as standard multi-point somatic prescriptions (e.g. LI4, PC6, ST36, SP6). Because trials administer combinations, statistical collinearity prevents isolating the independent contribution of any single acupoint in study-level meta-regression.

forestPlotHelper.title: How to Read this Forest Plot
forestPlotHelper.item1: Marker (Square/Circle): The estimated treatment effect for each study. Marker area reflects its statistical weight in the random-effects meta-analysis.
forestPlotHelper.item2: Horizontal Line: 95% confidence interval for each study, showing uncertainty around the study estimate.
forestPlotHelper.item3: Diamond: The pooled average treatment effect. The center indicates the point estimate and lateral tips represent the 95% confidence interval.
forestPlotHelper.item4: Vertical Dashed Line (0 or 1): The line of no effect. For mean differences (MD), values to the left of 0 favor TEAS/EA (reduced opioid or pain). For risk ratios (RR), values to the left of 1.0 favor TEAS/EA (lower incidence).
forestPlotHelper.item5: Prediction Interval: The dashed/extended bracket representing the estimated range of true effects that could plausibly occur in a future study or comparable clinical setting.

gradeHelper.high: High Certainty: Very confident that the true effect lies close to the estimate.
gradeHelper.moderate: Moderate Certainty: Moderately confident in effect estimate; true effect likely close, but could differ.
gradeHelper.low: Low Certainty: Confidence in effect estimate is limited; true effect may be substantially different.
gradeHelper.veryLow: Very Low Certainty: Very little confidence in effect estimate; true effect likely substantially different.
gradeHelper.rob: Risk of Bias: Assesses potential methodological bias affecting contributing trials.
gradeHelper.inconsistency: Inconsistency: Assesses unexplained heterogeneity and variance across study results.
gradeHelper.indirectness: Indirectness: Assesses differences in populations, interventions, or outcomes relative to review question.
gradeHelper.imprecision: Imprecision: Assesses uncertainty and width of confidence intervals relative to clinical decision thresholds.
gradeHelper.pubBias: Publication Bias: Assesses potential selective publication of positive or statistically significant findings.

interpretations.primary24h: Across the 11 analyzable trials, perioperative electrical acupoint stimulation reduced 24-hour postoperative opioid consumption by an average of 5.04 mg IV morphine equivalents (p = 0.0395). While statistically detectable, the pooled average is below the primary prespecified clinical importance threshold of 10 mg IV MME. The wide 95% prediction interval ([−18.33, +8.26] mg) crosses zero, showing that effect sizes vary substantially and clinical benefit is largest in procedures with high baseline opioid demand.
interpretations.teasStratum: In the double-blind sham-controlled TEAS stratum (k = 8 trials), opioid sparing averaged 2.40 mg IV MME (Knapp–Hartung 95% CI [−5.76, +0.95], p = 0.134). This reflects surgical case-mix: trials in minor ambulatory procedures showed minimal sparing (0.3–1.1 mg), whereas high-pain thoracotomy and abdominal trials achieved 12–21 mg sparing.
interpretations.eaStratum: In the needle electroacupuncture stratum (k = 3 trials), opioid sparing averaged 10.40 mg IV MME (p = 0.228). This estimate is strongly influenced by open-heart surgery (Coura 2011), where baseline opioid demand was 114 mg MME and sparing was 22.4 mg. Due to small study count (k = 3), this finding is descriptive.
interpretations.opioid48h: At 48 hours postoperatively (k = 7 trials), cumulative opioid reduction averaged 9.17 mg IV MME (95% CI [−17.15, −1.20], p = 0.030). Prolonged multi-phase stimulation demonstrated sustained opioid-sparing into the second postoperative day.
interpretations.baselineDemand: Across the included studies, higher opioid consumption in comparator groups was associated with greater estimated opioid sparing from TEAS/EA (β = −0.170, p = 0.0186, R² = 49.08%). Each additional 10 mg of baseline opioid demand was associated with approximately 1.7 mg greater opioid sparing. This is a study-level association and does not establish that changing opioid consumption in an individual patient causes TEAS/EA to become more effective.
interpretations.publicationYear: Later publication year was associated with smaller estimated opioid-sparing effects (β = +0.471 per year, p = 0.0287, R² = 82.81%). Possible explanations include secular changes over time in perioperative analgesic practice, multimodal ERAS protocols (e.g. regional blocks, NSAIDs, dexamethasone), surgical case mix, study methodology, comparator treatment, or other secular trends. The meta-regression cannot determine which mechanism caused the association.
interpretations.modalityMultivar: The apparent raw difference between EA and TEAS (unadjusted 5.98 mg) was attenuated after adjustment for baseline surgical opioid demand (adjusted β = +1.489 mg, p = 0.781). This confirms that differing baseline surgical pain intensity accounts for the observed cross-study variance rather than needle insertion alone.
interpretations.sexModerator: No evidence of an association between the study-level proportion of female participants and treatment effect was detected (β = −0.0128, p = 0.875, R² = 0.00%). This study-level finding does not establish equivalent treatment effects between individual women and men. Individual patient data (IPD) analysis is required to evaluate sex differences without ecological bias.
interpretations.primaryOpioid: Across the 11 analyzable trials, perioperative electrical acupoint stimulation reduced 24-hour postoperative opioid consumption by an average of 5.04 mg IV morphine equivalents (p = 0.0395). While statistically detectable, the pooled average is below the primary prespecified clinical importance threshold of 10 mg IV MME. tooltip.reml: Restricted Maximum Likelihood: Estimator used in primary random-effects meta-analysis to estimate between-study variance (τ²).
tooltip.knappHartung: Knapp–Hartung adjustment: Provides robust standard errors and confidence intervals in random-effects meta-analysis, especially with limited study counts.
tooltip.i2: I² statistic: Percentage of variability in effect estimates due to between-study heterogeneity rather than sampling chance.
tooltip.metaRegressionR2: Meta-regression R²: Proportion of between-study variance accounted for by the moderator; not individual patient variance.
